topic_tag: a small press and a poetry movement
prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
blank_sentence: One historian of the town's literary life argues that the press ______ the plain-spoken regional poetry that flourished there in the 1920s.

worlds.passage: Early in the last century, a one-room press in a river town printed poetry in editions of a few hundred copies. It opened in 1919, when the local poets had already begun writing in that style, and its editor printed whatever they brought him without changing a line; he let them hold their meetings and readings in the room above the shop, and the group, which met nowhere else, grew quickly there. One historian of the town's literary life argues that the press ______ the plain-spoken regional poetry that flourished there in the 1920s.
worlds.explanation: The poets met and read only in the room above the shop, so the press "housed" the movement. "Hindered" fails because the group grew quickly there; "heralded" fails because the poets had already begun before the press opened; "guided" fails because the editor printed their work without changing a line.

hindered.why: the movement flourished rather than being held back

heralded.quote: had already begun writing in that style
heralded.why: the press did not announce something not yet arrived

guided.why: an editor who never intervenes does not direct the poets

worlds.passage: Early in the last century, a one-room press in a river town printed poetry in editions of a few hundred copies. It opened in 1919, when the local poets had already begun writing in that style, but its editor refused to print unrhymed verse and bought up the town's only other press; the poets, who met in a cafe across the river, kept writing unrhymed verse anyway and waited years for their first books. One historian of the town's literary life argues that the press ______ the plain-spoken regional poetry that flourished there in the 1920s.
worlds.explanation: By refusing their verse and buying the only other press, the editor made the poets wait years for books, so the press "hindered" the movement. "Housed" fails because the poets met in a cafe across the river; "heralded" fails because they had already begun before it opened; "guided" fails because they kept writing unrhymed verse anyway, unswayed by him.

housed.quote: met in a cafe across the river
housed.why: the movement had its home elsewhere

heralded.quote: had already begun writing in that style

guided.why: the poets did not follow its direction

worlds.passage: Early in the last century, a one-room press in a river town printed poetry in editions of a few hundred copies. In 1909 its editor printed an essay calling for poems in the plain speech of the river towns, the very style local poets would adopt a decade later, but the press closed in 1910, before any of them had begun to write, and none of them read the essay until a librarian found it in 1930. One historian of the town's literary life argues that the press ______ the plain-spoken regional poetry that flourished there in the 1920s.
worlds.explanation: The 1909 essay announced the style years before the poets arrived at it, so the press "heralded" the movement. "Housed" and "hindered" fail because the press closed in 1910, before any of the poets had begun, so it could neither shelter nor obstruct them; "guided" fails because none of them read the essay until 1930.

housed.quote: closed in 1910, before any of them had begun
housed.why: a press gone before the movement could not be its home

hindered.why: a closed press could not obstruct poets who came later

guided.quote: none of them read the essay until
guided.why: poets who never saw its call were not steered by it

worlds.passage: Early in the last century, a one-room press in a river town printed poetry in editions of a few hundred copies. It opened in 1919, when the local poets had only begun experimenting, and its editor returned every manuscript with pages of notes urging plainer speech and local subjects; the poets, who met in a cafe across the river, rewrote their poems along those lines, and a city firm published their books to quick success. One historian of the town's literary life argues that the press ______ the plain-spoken regional poetry that flourished there in the 1920s.
worlds.explanation: The editor's notes urged plainer speech, and the poets rewrote their poems along those lines, so the press "guided" the movement. "Housed" fails because the poets met in a cafe across the river and published with a city firm; "hindered" fails because their books met quick success; "heralded" fails because the poets were already experimenting when the press opened.

housed.quote: met in a cafe across the river
housed.why: the press was not the movement's home

hindered.why: the movement was not held back

heralded.why: the poets had already started, so the press did not announce them in advance
